briefs.brief_cn: DoorDash 是餐饮外卖需求、配送密度、会员频次和商户数字化变现的关键观察点。卡点假设是：如果消费者仍愿意为便利支付溢价、DashPass 能提高频次并降低流失、商户广告和平台服务能在不明显损害商户经济性的情况下扩张，则 DoorDash 可能成为餐饮非堂食需求的基础设施型节点。现有公开证据显示，2026 年一季度总订单同比增长 27%，美国餐饮品类新消费者和成熟用户订单率均同比增长，DashPass 会员增长和流失改善。但仍需拆分餐饮与杂货、本地商业、Wolt/Deliveroo 等非纯餐饮贡献，核验餐饮 take rate、广告收入占比、商户留存和监管劳工成本影响。
briefs.brief_en: DoorDash is a high-signal node for off-premise restaurant demand, logistics density, subscription-driven frequency, and merchant monetization. The chokepoint hypothesis is that if consumers continue to pay for convenience, DashPass supports repeat ordering and lower churn, and merchant ads/services scale without breaking restaurant economics, DoorDash can function as infrastructure for restaurant demand outside the dining room. Current public evidence shows Q1 2026 total orders grew 27% year over year, U.S. restaurant new consumers and mature-cohort order rates grew year over year, and DashPass member trends improved. The key gap is isolating restaurant delivery from grocery, broader local commerce, Wolt/Deliveroo, and other non-restaurant contributions.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: DoorDash may be a demand-discovery and last-mile density chokepoint for restaurants: it concentrates consumer demand, logistics capacity, membership frequency, and merchant advertising surfaces that individual restaurants may struggle to replicate at scale.
evidence_to_verify: Q1 2026 total orders increased to 933 million, up 27% year over year, per DoorDash Form 10-Q.
Q1 2026 U.S. restaurant category showed year-over-year growth in new consumers and mature-cohort order rates, per DoorDash shareholder materials.
DashPass member growth accelerated in Q1 2026 with stronger sign-ups and reduced churn, per DoorDash shareholder materials.
Verify restaurant-specific GOV, take rate, ads contribution, merchant retention/churn, and order frequency separate from grocery, convenience, Wolt, Deliveroo, and broader local commerce.
falsification: Restaurant-specific order growth decelerates materially while non-restaurant categories drive reported growth.
Merchant churn rises or take-rate/advertising monetization pressures restaurant margins enough to reduce platform participation.
DashPass engagement weakens, member churn rises, or mature-cohort frequency stalls.
Regulatory labor-cost changes materially impair contribution profit or force higher consumer fees that reduce demand.
monitoring_items: Restaurant-only order growth and GOV disclosure, if available
Net revenue margin and contribution profit as a percentage of Marketplace GOV
DashPass member growth, churn, and order frequency
Advertising revenue growth and merchant adoption
Courier labor classification, minimum-pay rules, and fee-cap/regulatory developments
Mix shift between restaurants, grocery, convenience, Wolt, Deliveroo, and other local-commerce categories

briefs.brief_cn: Yum! Brands 是全球加盟制 QSR 系统的关键样本，尤其能观察 Taco Bell 的价值定位、菜单创新、数字化和国际扩张是否能抵消 Pizza Hut 的结构性压力。卡点假设是：Yum 的多品牌、全球加盟、技术平台和门店开发能力构成可复制的 QSR 增长系统。公开证据显示，2026 年一季度全球同店销售增长 3%，系统销售按固定汇率增长 6%，Taco Bell 美国同店销售增长 8%，数字系统销售接近 110 亿美元且占系统销售 63%。但品牌组合复杂，Pizza Hut 疲弱可能稀释 Taco Bell/KFC 的强信号。
briefs.brief_en: Yum! Brands is a global franchised QSR read-through, especially for whether Taco Bell’s value proposition, menu innovation, digital engagement, and international growth can offset structural pressure at Pizza Hut. The chokepoint hypothesis is that Yum’s multi-brand franchise architecture, technology platform, and unit-development engine form a repeatable QSR growth system. Public evidence shows Q1 2026 worldwide same-store sales rose 3%, system sales grew 6% excluding FX, Taco Bell U.S. same-store sales rose 8%, and digital system sales approached $11 billion, representing 63% of system sales. The main complication is brand-mix complexity, with Pizza Hut weakness potentially diluting the Taco Bell/KFC signal.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: Yum may be a franchised QSR operating-system chokepoint: brand scale, franchise economics, technology, and global unit development can compound if franchisees continue to earn acceptable returns and digital systems raise throughput and frequency.
evidence_to_verify: Q1 2026 worldwide same-store sales grew 3% and system sales grew 6% excluding foreign exchange.
Taco Bell U.S. same-store sales grew 8% in Q1 2026.
Digital system sales neared $11 billion and reached 63% of system sales in Q1 2026.
Verify Taco Bell versus KFC versus Pizza Hut traffic, franchisee profitability, royalty growth, unit economics, and promotional margin impact.
falsification: Taco Bell comps become primarily price-driven while traffic weakens.
Pizza Hut underperformance consumes management attention or capital and offsets Taco Bell/KFC growth.
Franchisee unit economics deteriorate, slowing net unit growth or increasing closures.
Digital mix grows but fails to improve throughput, labor efficiency, ticket size, or loyalty frequency.
monitoring_items: Brand-level same-store sales and traffic, especially Taco Bell U.S.
Franchisee restaurant-level margins and unit economics
Net unit growth, closures, and remodel requirements
Pizza Hut strategic review and closure cadence
Digital system sales mix, loyalty engagement, drive-thru throughput, and AI/technology rollout
Promotional intensity and value-menu margin impact

briefs.brief_cn: Texas Roadhouse 是休闲餐饮中少数能直接检验正客流、价值感和门店执行力的高纯度样本。卡点假设是：在消费者更谨慎、牛肉和人工成本仍有压力的环境下，Texas Roadhouse 依靠高性价比、门店吞吐、等待需求和稳定执行力，可能继续获得客流份额。公开证据显示，2026 年一季度可比餐厅销售增长 7.1%，其中客流增长 4.5%、平均客单增长 2.6%；餐厅利润率为 16.3%，受 6.2% 商品通胀和 3.8% 工资及其他人工通胀影响。核心验证点是正客流是否能持续，而不是仅靠涨价。
briefs.brief_en: Texas Roadhouse is a high-purity casual-dining test case for positive traffic, value perception, and store-level execution. The chokepoint hypothesis is that in a cautious consumer environment with beef and labor pressure, Texas Roadhouse can continue taking traffic share through perceived value, throughput, wait-list demand, and consistent operations. Public evidence shows Q1 2026 comparable restaurant sales rose 7.1%, driven by 4.5% traffic growth and 2.6% average-check growth; restaurant margin was 16.3%, pressured by 6.2% commodity inflation and 3.8% wage/other labor inflation. The key test is whether traffic remains positive rather than comps being sustained mostly by pricing.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: Texas Roadhouse may be a casual-dining demand-share chokepoint: its value perception and operating throughput can attract traffic even when consumers trade down or resist price increases.
evidence_to_verify: Q1 2026 comparable restaurant sales rose 7.1%, with traffic up 4.5% and average check up 2.6%.
Q1 2026 restaurant margin decreased 36 basis points to 16.3%.
Q1 2026 commodity inflation was 6.2%, driven partly by higher beef costs, and wage/other labor inflation was 3.8%.
Verify wait-time data, throughput, guest satisfaction, beef-cost outlook, labor productivity, and whether positive traffic continues after menu-price actions.
falsification: Traffic turns negative while comparable sales depend mostly on pricing.
Beef inflation persists or accelerates enough to compress restaurant margins materially.
Labor inflation and staffing constraints reduce service quality or throughput.
Value perception weakens as menu prices rise relative to QSR and other casual-dining alternatives.
monitoring_items: Traffic versus check split in comparable sales
Beef, commodity, and wage inflation outlook
Restaurant margin and labor percentage of sales
Average weekly sales, table turns, wait times, and throughput metrics
Menu pricing cadence and consumer value scores
New-unit productivity and cannibalization risk

briefs.brief_cn: Chipotle 是高端快休闲的吞吐、数字订单和品牌定价能力基准。卡点假设是：如果 Chipotle 能在不依赖过度涨价的情况下恢复交易量，并通过数字化、设备效率、菜单创新和门店扩张维持利润率，则它仍是快休闲效率模型的代表。但当前证据更偏“需验证”：2026 年一季度收入增长 7.4% 至约 31 亿美元，可比餐厅销售仅增长 0.5%，交易量增长 0.6%、平均客单下降 0.1%，数字销售占食品饮料收入 38.6%。这说明交易量回正但增速较低，市场需验证其高估值质量是否仍由真实流量支撑。
briefs.brief_en: Chipotle is a benchmark for premium fast-casual throughput, digital ordering, and brand pricing power. The chokepoint hypothesis is that if Chipotle can restore transaction growth without relying excessively on price, while using digital systems, equipment efficiency, menu innovation, and unit growth to protect margins, it remains a leading fast-casual operating model. Current evidence is more mixed: Q1 2026 revenue rose 7.4% to about $3.1 billion, comparable restaurant sales increased only 0.5%, transactions rose 0.6%, average check declined 0.1%, and digital sales represented 38.6% of food and beverage revenue. The key question is whether quality is still supported by real traffic rather than historical reputation and valuation premium.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: Chipotle may be a premium fast-casual throughput chokepoint: brand, kitchen process, digital ordering, and high-unit-volume economics can create a scalable restaurant model if transaction growth and margins recover together.
evidence_to_verify: Q1 2026 revenue rose 7.4% to approximately $3.1 billion.
Q1 2026 comparable restaurant sales increased 0.5%, driven by transactions up 0.6% and average check down 0.1%.
Q1 2026 digital sales represented 38.6% of total food and beverage revenue.
Verify labor productivity, restaurant-level margin, protein/input inflation, digital order accuracy, throughput initiatives, loyalty engagement, and 2026 comparable-sales guidance.
falsification: Transaction growth falls back into negative territory or remains too weak to support unit economics.
Comparable sales rely mainly on price while traffic and value perception deteriorate.
Digital mix stays high but creates order-accuracy, throughput, or guest-satisfaction problems.
Protein, wage, or freight inflation compresses restaurant margins faster than productivity initiatives can offset.
monitoring_items: Traffic versus price/check split in comparable sales
Restaurant-level operating margin and labor productivity
Digital sales mix, order accuracy, app/loyalty engagement, and delivery aggregator mix
Throughput metrics and high-efficiency equipment rollout
Food inflation, especially beef, chicken, avocado, dairy, and freight
New restaurant openings, average unit volumes, and returns on new units

key_points: Q1 2026 total orders increased to 933 million, up 27% year over year.
Marketplace GOV definition includes taxes, tips, applicable consumer fees, and membership fees related to DashPass, Wolt+, and Deliveroo Plus.
DoorDash stated that U.S. restaurant new consumers and mature-cohort order rates grew year over year in Q1 2026.
DoorDash stated that DashPass member trends accelerated, with stronger sign-ups and reduced churn.
Taco Bell U.S. same-store sales grew 8%.
System sales grew 6% excluding foreign exchange.
Brand-level data shows divergence across KFC, Taco Bell, and Pizza Hut.
Useful for monitoring same-store sales by brand and geography.
Restaurant margin was 16.3%, down 36 basis points.
Commodity inflation was 6.2% and wage/other labor inflation was 3.8%.
Higher beef costs were a driver of commodity inflation.
Restaurant labor expenses as a percentage of restaurant and other sales declined to 32.9% in Q1 2026 from 33.3% in Q1 2025.
Q1 2026 revenue increased 7.4% to approximately $3.1 billion.
Digital sales represented 38.6% of total food and beverage revenue.
Comparable restaurant sales increased 0.5%, driven by 0.6% transaction growth and partially offset by a 0.1% decrease in average check.
Digital sales represented 38.6% of total food and beverage revenue.

memory_update.note: For DASH, treat restaurant-specific purity as the central evidence gap; aggregate order growth is not sufficient because grocery, convenience, Wolt, Deliveroo, and local commerce can dilute the restaurant signal.

For YUM, the strongest positive signal is Taco Bell U.S. momentum and digital system scale, but Pizza Hut weakness and brand-mix complexity should cap thesis confidence until brand-level traffic and franchisee economics are verified.
For TXRH, the decisive metric is traffic-led comparable sales under beef and wage inflation. A shift from traffic-led comps to price-led comps would downgrade the thesis.
For CMG, the key debate is whether premium fast-casual quality is still supported by durable transaction growth and throughput productivity. Current Q1 2026 comps are positive but modest.

summary: Layer 4 ranked-candidate briefs for the Restaurants theme, focused on four mid-ranked but high-signal public-market nodes: DoorDash as off-premise demand/logistics-density infrastructure, Yum! Brands as global franchised QSR/value-and-digital read-through, Texas Roadhouse as casual-dining traffic/value test case, and Chipotle as premium fast-casual throughput/digital benchmark. These are research-priority briefs only, not investment recommendations.
